newsitem.title: USA: Florida ruling hurts Engle tobacco suit - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Florida ruling hurts Engle tobacco suit - lawyer.

text.p: A Miami lawyer suing the major tobacco companies on behalf of thousands of Florida smokers said on Friday his case had been damaged by a partial summary judgment stripping away some claims against the industry.

The ruling Friday by Dade Circuit Judge Alan Postman was issued in response to claims by tobacco companies that some facets of the plaintiffs' case in a smokers' class-action lawsuit, known as Engle vs R.J. Reynolds, should be pre-empted.
The landmark lawsuit, seeking damages on behalf of 400,000 to 500,000 Florida cigarette smokers, was named after Dr. Howard Engle, a Miami physician stricken by emphysema.

"We're hurt. There is much in this order that hurts us," plaintiffs' attorney Stanley Rosenblatt said of the ruling, issued at the end of a pretrial hearing in the Engle case, which is scheduled for trial on September 8.

"Anything that restricts our ability to tell the American people the full story about the decades-long pattern of fraud and concealment on the part of the tobacco industry is a crippling blow," Rosenblatt said.
Robert Heim, an attorney for Philip Morris, said "we feel good" about the pre-emptions but declined further comment until he had read the full ruling.
Postman ruled that 36 of the 58 claims challenged by the tobacco companies were pre-empted.

At a hearing March 21, the tobacco companies argued that many plaintiffs' claims should be pre-empted on the basis of a U.S. Supreme Court ruling in the landmark 1988 Cipollone tobacco case. The ruling interpreted pre-emption provisions of the 1969 Public Health Cigarette Smoking Act and the 1965 Federal Cigarette Labeling and Advertising Act.
Rosenblatt said among the claims Postman ordered pre-empted was the argument that the tobacco industry had targeted teen-agers, women and minorities through its advertising.

Postman also struck a paragraph in which the plaintiffs claimed the industry lied through "a multimillion-dollar campaign pretending that the Council for Tobacco Research is impartial," Rosenblatt said.
"He wrongly read the Cipollone case," Rosenblatt said. "He has extended the pre-emptions in the Engle case far beyond any fair reading of the Cipollone case."
Rosenblatt said he would still be able to make a very strong case against the industry's "history of fraud," despite the ruling.
"It's a battle; it's not the war," he said.

Defendants in the Engle suit include Philip Morris Cos Inc, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, Lorillard Tobacco Co, a unit of Loews Corp, and Liggett Group Inc, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd.
